title: The Levites' tithes as God's portion
english: “Take away from it an offering” (Numbers 18:26). Those who were called to serve as priests according to the law of Moses received tithes from the sons of Israel as their portion and inheritance from God.
translator_notes: The Greek text appears to be a fragment, cut off at the end of the sentence.
No obvious OCR errors or debris were found in the source text.
baehrens: PG 69; Fragmenta duo in Numeros frag rem early
orientation: Cyril is opening his commentary on Numbers by quoting the command about the offering and explaining that the Levitical priests received tithes from Israel as their share from God.

title: The Levites' Tenth to Aaron as a Type of Christ
english: They themselves offered the tithe to the one who presided over and led the priesthood, that is, to Aaron. He has been set as a type of Christ, ministering not in the first tabernacle, the one that has its standing place, but in the inner and hidden one. “Take the rod and assemble the congregation” (Numbers 20:8).

orientation: Cyril is explaining how the Levitical priests, after receiving tithes from Israel, in turn offered a tenth to Aaron, the head of the priesthood, who prefigures Christ.

title: The rod as confirmation of faith and Christ as rock
english: Observe that, to confirm their faith, he recalls the wonders in Egypt, saying, “Take the rod in your hand, with which you struck the river” (Exodus 17:5). And soon after: Christ is compared to a rock because of its unbreakable and unshakable nature.
